author: y. e. mayo
title: Easton Key names Taylor Boggs assistant men's golf coach at Austin Peay
text:
Austin Peay State University’s head men’s golf coach Easton Key named Taylor Boggs as the Governors’ assistant men’s golf coach ahead of the 2026-27 season, according to a June 3 announcement.
Boggs joins Austin Peay from Itawamba Community College, where he served as head coach for the past four seasons. During his tenure with the Indians, he helped develop players for opportunities beyond junior college and saw five golfers advance their careers to higher levels. Three of his players also qualified for NJCAA Regionals as individuals.
Prior to his time at Itawamba Community College, Boggs was an assistant coach at Delta State during the 2019-20 season. While there, he contributed to coaching Zack Zediker, who won the Jack Nicklaus Award—one of college golf’s top individual honors.
Boggs brings collegiate playing experience from two seasons at Louisiana-Monroe between 2011 and 2013 after a notable junior and high school career with Itawamba Agricultural High School. He earned multiple wins on the MJGA and Coca-Cola Junior Tours and achieved several top-five finishes on tours such as SJGT, Hurricane Junior Tour, and Arrowhead Junior Tour. As a high school golfer, Boggs won three state championships in Mississippi’s 4-A division in 2007, 2009, and 2010 before finishing runner-up in 2011.
A native of Fulton, Mississippi, Boggs earned a bachelor’s degree in kinesiology from Mississippi State University in 2017 and later completed a master’s degree in sport and human performance from Delta State University in 2020.
